absent_coverage: The passive-skew (ll/hh) axis is covered only as a separately-recorded supplement on tt MOS (ll/hh x 3 temperatures); combined MOS-corner x resistor-skew points (e.g. ss MOS with res_high) are NOT run -- sky130.lib.spice has no such combined section and no multi-section bundle was built for this campaign.

Mismatch Monte Carlo is run only as the `--axis mc` supplement: the real-bias-core variant, tt/ss sections, -40/27/125 C, at the 100 V/s primary rate, N = 20 per corner (see the monte_carlo block). NOT sampled by it: the ideal-bias variant, the ff/sf/fs sections, the ll/hh passive-skew axis, global process MC, and mismatch on the post-layout extracted netlist. The corner-matrix numbers remain corner values of the nominal drawn circuit.
Sweep rates other than 100 V/s (and its 50 V/s guard) are not simulated; supply-ramp-rate sensitivity of the assembled block is covered by sim/supply-ramp-top.
Post-layout parasitics are not included (schematic-level netlist).
The ideal-bias variant uses a constant 1 uA IBIAS and a 1.25 V VREF at every corner; real bias_core spread is only shown by the separately-reported real-bias-core variant.

definitions.BIAS_OK asserted (diagnostic): at the sweep peak, v(bias_ok) >= 0.9 x the at-peak supply -- a rail swing; a diagnostic label on recorded evidence, the raw per-sample max and at-peak values are recorded beside every label (issue #401). BIAS_OK follows VDD through bias_core's weak XMO1P pullup whenever the NOKX pulldown is off, so a max-over-sweep test cannot distinguish assertion
definitions.CMPO released (diagnostic): max v(xdut.cmpo) over the sweep >= 0.5 V; while it is below, XMDCMPO holds CMPO at VSS (the clamp) when BIAS_OKB is high (issue #401)
definitions.VPOR-up / VPOR-down: interpolated VDD at which POR_RAW crosses 0.5*VDD (POR_RAW high = above half the instantaneous supply) during the UP / DOWN segment; segments split at the VDD maximum; state evaluated only for VDD >= 1.0 V
definitions.binding corner: the process/temperature point that sets the minimum or maximum of each metric over the corners with a clean, rate-consistent result
definitions.edge extraction: VDD sample step <= 10 mV around an edge, linear interpolation inside the bracket; POR_RAW state evaluated for VDD >= 1 V only
definitions.hysteresis: VPOR-up - VPOR-down at the same process/temperature
definitions.mismatch sample: One klt sim request per (process, temperature) with a monte_carlo block (vary=mismatch on the _mm process sections, local mismatch only), --backend batch through sim_common's shared submit path with batch.capacity_wait_s set; never a local grid. Each sample is a full transient VDD sweep -- the measurement IS the sweep, so a temperature cannot share another temperature's realisation -- and returns its own waveform, from which threshold_extractor.py extracts that sample's VPOR-up / VPOR-down / hysteresis.
definitions.no transition: a segment in which POR_RAW does not change state is reported as no_transition (with the state it stayed in), not omitted; hysteresis is then NO_RESULT
definitions.quasi-static guard: VPOR-up and VPOR-down at the primary rate must agree with the half-rate sweep within 10 mV (stated tolerance, chosen for this campaign, not ratified); otherwise the corner is reported RATE-DEPENDENT and excluded from the binding-corner table
definitions.resolution: an edge is accepted only if the two samples bracketing it differ by <= 10 mV of VDD; otherwise UNRESOLVED
definitions.stuck class: mechanism class of a failed-release realisation from its diagnostics: enable-clamp (BIAS_OK never asserted), comparator-stuck (BIAS_OK asserted, CMPO never rose), extractor-miss (both released yet graded no_transition); None = no diagnostic data
definitions.sweep peak: t = tstop/2 of the 100 V/s triangle, where VDD reaches its 3.63 V peak; at-peak values are linearly interpolated at that time

monte_carlo.request_sizing: One klt sim request per (process, temperature) = 6 requests, N = 20 mismatch samples each, at the primary 100 V/s rate. Sizing arithmetic: the measured worst-corner cost of the real-bias-core 100 V/s grid is 142 s (corners/20261009-054331-79eebd4-real-bias-core/r100/klt-report.json, per-corner runtime_s; the 15-corner request summed to 1924 s), so one request is 20 x 142 s = 2840 s of serial fleet wall clock, 21% under the fleet's 3600 s per-job ceiling; N = 24 would sit at 3408 s inside the same ceiling and N = 20 is the recorded choice with the larger headroom (the sigma resolution at N = 20 is 16.2%). Folding the three temperatures into one request would be 60 x 142 s = 8520 s -> batch_job_timeout, the exact failure sim/temp-core-accuracy-mc recorded for its first 3000-unit requests.
monte_carlo.seed_offsets: Seed for request k = seed + k, k = 1..6 in (process, temperature) order: tt/-40C -> 20261115, tt/27C -> 20261116, tt/125C -> 20261117, ss/-40C -> 20261118, ss/27C -> 20261119, ss/125C -> 20261120. klt derives each sample's seed from the corner index (0 inside every one-corner request here), so a shared base seed across the six requests would re-draw the SAME realisations in each; the distinct offsets keep the six realisation sets independent. Each sample's own derived seed is recorded per sample in the record.
monte_carlo.statistical_convention: Per corner: mean and sample sigma (Bessel, n-1) of VPOR-up, VPOR-down and hysteresis over the valid Monte Carlo samples; hysteresis is computed PER SAMPLE (VPOR-up - VPOR-down of ONE realisation), never combined from the two marginal sigmas (comparator offset moves both edges of one realisation in the same direction, so the marginal combination overstates the hysteresis spread). The statistical resolution of a corner's sigma is stated as 1/sqrt(2(N_valid - 1)) of its valid N (16.2% at N = 20). Samples graded no_transition, multiple_transitions, unresolved or wrong_direction are excluded AND counted, never silently dropped; an all-invalid corner renders a three-state NO-RESULT, never sigma = 0. NOT sampled: global process Monte Carlo (MC_PR_SWITCH), the 50 V/s half-rate guard (the MC points are unguarded), the ideal-bias variant, the ff/sf/fs sections, the ll/hh passive-skew axis, and post-layout parasitics. Temperatures draw INDEPENDENT realisation sets (one transient per temperature, one realisation set per request), so per-corner statistics are valid and NO per-sample temperature-drift or temperature-correlation claim is made.

probe:
Local deterministic single-device sensitivity probes, one `ngspice -b` per point (issue #455 attribution cross-check; the statistical evidence is the fleet run above). Method: exactly ONE instance of the committed `design/netlist/bias_core.spice` is swapped for a diagnostic copy of the sky130 `g5v0d10v5` subckt that adds a deterministic `dv` to the mismatch `delvto` term (PDK mismatch otherwise OFF, `MC_MM_SWITCH=0`); the cell is started with a physical 0 -> 3.3 V ramp (`tran ... uic`, `reltol=1e-4`) and BIAS_OK / NOKO / NOKX are read at the end of the ramp. `dv` is expressed in units of the swapped device's own mismatch sigma, from the PDK coefficients (`sw_mm_vth0` = 8.2 mV.um for NFET, 12.0 mV.um for PFET, over sqrt(W*L)).

Healthy operating point at the asserted state (tt/27 C, 3.3 V): V(NBTOP)-V(NA) = **2.75 mV** is the detector's entire input signal; TOK = 1.956 V, NOKL = 0.749 V, NOKO = 1.498 V, NOKX = 1.8 mV, NKG ~ 0 V; pair currents 32.7/32.1 nA (difference 0.59 nA = the signal current), mirror XML/XMOL currents 32.1/32.7 nA, XMOK2 sinking XMOK2P's 67.7 nA with NOKX at 1.8 mV.

Results (tt/27 C and ss/27 C; `+`/`-` rows of one device are the NOKO-starving vs NOKO-feeding direction):

| device (sigma) | -3 sigma | -1 sigma | +1 sigma | +3 sigma |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| XMOL1, mirror diode (2.90 mV) | OK | OK | OK (NOKX degraded to 36 mV) | **FAIL** (NOKO 0.14 V, NOKX railed) |
| XMOL2, mirror output (2.90 mV) | **FAIL** (NOKO 0.14 V) | OK (NOKX 38 mV) | OK | OK |
| XMOKA, input pair (2.12 mV) | **FAIL** (NOKO 0.17 V) | OK (NOKX 13 mV) | OK | OK |
| XMOKB, input pair (2.12 mV) | OK | OK | OK (NOKX 13 mV) | **FAIL** (NOKO 0.17 V) |
| XMOK2, NOKX pulldown (2.90 mV) | OK | OK | OK | OK (NOKX 1.8 mV) |
| XMOK2P, NOKX pullup (6.00 mV) | OK | OK | OK | OK (NOKX 2.3 mV) |
| XML1/XML2, error-amp load mirror (1.45 mV) | OK | OK | OK | OK (VREF moves, BIAS_OK holds) |

(same FAIL pattern at ss/27 C for XMOL1 +3 sigma / XMOL2 -3 sigma: NOKO 0.14 V, NOKX railed, VREF 1.25675 V unchanged.)

Reading: the output stage (XMOK2 vs XMOK2P) is INSENSITIVE at +-3 sigma -- the ratio-fight hypothesis for this failure is refuted. The **first stage** carries the whole defect: a single XMOL1/XMOL2 draw of +3/-3 sigma, or a single XMOKA/XMOKB draw of -3/+3 sigma, in the NOKO-starving direction, collapses NOKO to ~0.14-0.17 V and BIAS_OK never asserts, with VREF unmoved (the detector sits outside the regulation loop). At +-1 sigma the assertion survives but NOKX degrades from 1.8 mV to 13-38 mV -- the nominal margin is already spent by ONE device at ONE sigma against a 2.75 mV signal. Under the Monte Carlo, where XMOL1+XMOL2+XMOKA+XMOKB draw simultaneously (input-referred combined offset sigma ~5-14 mV over the corner/temperature set), the detector is a coin flip weighted by a 0.2-0.6 sigma signal -- matching the recorded 38/120 non-release rate. The devices responsible are the OK-detector first stage: **XMOL1/XMOL2 (dominant: 2.90 mV sigma each, in weak inversion) and XMOKA/XMOKB (secondary: 2.12 mV sigma each)**.
